correctness.rationale: For all m>=2, n=1 gives L(j)=1 and kappa(j)=j in Theorem 1.3 of arXiv:2505.20489. Collecting the five numerator sums produces the exact reciprocal coefficient vector. Comparing all Fourier coefficients against d+(d+2)|S_d|^2+|S_(d+1)|^2 proves positivity on every unit-circle point for every d. Reciprocal pairing counts the d interior roots; explicit points and a nonvanishing denominator realize them as Bergman zeros. Four independent standard-library integer polynomial checks passed at every m=2..501; the proof is algebraic for arbitrary d.

originality.rationale: Theorem 1.7 and Section 4.3 of the full arXiv:2505.20489 / Math. Z. paper treat finitely many fixed differences and pose general circle nonvanishing as Conjecture 4.20. The 2016 and 2017 integer/general exponent studies supply numerator formulas and/or kernel-zero existence, not the exact interior zeros on s=t or a circle-square certificate; the 2023 monomial-polyhedra paper supplies a general kernel formula. The n=1 axis traverses unbounded gap m-1 and has an exact uniform proof. No checked published statement implies that conclusion; unindexed equivalence remains possible.

value.rationale: The exact number of diagonal roots for each integer index m is a natural infinite subfamily of an explicit 2025/2026 open root-location conjecture. Unlike known all-integer existence of a kernel zero, the result solves an unbounded-degree reciprocal-polynomial census on the same analytically defined locus, with an exact positive-squares certificate and no finite cutoff. This is substantive structural information rather than an arbitrary narrow numeric slice.
